o1.biggest_strength: The brilliant mitigation plan for the stockout gap, specifically the pro pre-order to protect bridal artists and honest alert buttons for everyday customers.
o1.biggest_mistake: Assuming the held stock was already included in the on-hand units. If added together (9,100 + 3,900), the stock lasts until December 8, completely eliminating the stockout gap.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Catching that the held stock was in addition to the on-hand stock, which would mean the rush order arrives just in time with no out-of-stock gap to mitigate.

o2.biggest_strength: The clear margin analysis on the Night-out kit bundle, which is a highly actionable way to turn slow-moving glitter palettes back into cash.
o2.biggest_mistake: Like the other draft, assuming held stock was part of the on-hand units instead of extra, thereby missing the fact that the gap could be closed entirely.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Noticing the math that 9,100 + 3,900 = 13,000 units covers the 21-day lead time for a rush order perfectly, and injecting a bit more of the brand's bold voice.

reason: Both missed that the warehouse stock was additive (which would have closed the gap), but Output 1 provided a vastly superior mitigation plan by directly targeting our high-value makeup artists and nailing the brand voice.
